timeline_utc.2026-09-27T17:10:39Z: re-confirmed live: cloudbilling.googleapis.com projects.getBillingInfo still reports billingEnabled=true; a fresh LOAD job and a fresh DML DELETE against a new non-streamed throwaway table (taal.zz_billing_probe2) both succeeded cleanly -- billing is stable, not intermittently recovering

root_cause: payment/billing-account verification issue, not a project-billing unlink and not an IAM change [Likely]. cloudbilling.googleapis.com projects.getBillingInfo showed billingEnabled: true throughout, including during the failures -- inconsistent with true BigQuery sandbox mode (no billing account at all). The project owner independently found the linked billing account flagged "overdue / needs valid payment information" and "must verify this account" in the Cloud Console; BigQuery appears to enforce a stricter, real payment-health check than the simple project-to-billing-account link cloudbilling.googleapis.com reports. Writes resumed working shortly after the owner addressed this (last confirmed failure job-level at 2026-09-27T15:31:09Z; recovery re-confirmed live at 2026-09-27T17:10:39Z, over an hour later, with billing still enabled and DML/LOAD both working -- this is a stable recovery, not a flapping one). IAM audit logs (SetIamPolicy, 3-day window) show no changes from any human account and none in the failure window -- ruling out an IAM-driven explanation. Billing-account-level audit events are not visible to the taal-deploy service account (PERMISSION_DENIED on billingAccounts.get), so the exact trigger on Google's side stays unconfirmed [Guessing]; only that it correlates with a payment/verification problem, and is now resolved, is well-supported.
superseded_finding: The original finding in this file ("BigQuery DML is blocked project-wide... SELECT and INSERT both work", later revised to "every write path is now blocked", with a likely_explanation of "a limited sandbox DML allowance that closed") is superseded. The "sandbox allowance" theory was never well-supported -- billingEnabled was true throughout, which sandbox mode does not allow -- and the block has since cleared, which a true sandbox-mode project could not do without a project owner explicitly linking a billing account for the first time (this project already had one linked).
